evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The current `manager_restarted` check still treats any PID and invocation-ID change as a manager restart, without requiring that both observations came from the same guest boot. A guest reboot changes both values, so a reboot can satisfy `manager_restarted`, and a later reboot can satisfy the separate `boot_id_changed` check. The existing boot-ID logic covers only the reboot check, so this is an ordinary false-positive defect in the feasibility evidence.
